events.credibility_reason: Content known only from conflicting secondary descriptions (generic equality vs upper bound); paper not read.
Single numerically computed attractor, known only from a search summary; a single non-generic example does not contradict the typical-system conjecture.
The 'direct computation' is not displayed; the product is non-generic and the step making failure generic is deferred; the KY remark is an aside not evidently refereed.
The general-failure sentence is uncited and the only candidate source is conditional; the preprint conceded other results incorrect in v2.

why: The only post-snapshot event bearing on truth is Wang–Cao–Zhao (ETDS, online 12 Feb 2024): a refereed theorem that the KY equality holds for SRB measures under additional conditions, a restriction of the statement, so case/digested/confirmed. Marin–Bonetto–Corsi is dated by its 2023 v1 (the 2024 revision generalised the main analyticity theorem, not the KY remark), so it is pre-snapshot; its product example contradicts an 'every attractor' reading but not the typical-system one, so case/refuted with doubt. Disca merely asserts an uncited claim and is none; its Gemini use (scripts, editing, references, preliminary checking) is not mathematics. Numerical comparisons (Hoover group, Lin–Chua) are instances; Parker–Goluskin, Le and Bakri–Verhulst apply or estimate the formula and are none. Ledrappier is scored bound since one secondary reading makes it an inequality D ≤ D_KY rather than a settled case.
doubts: Wang–Cao–Zhao's additional conditions are unknown, so the size of the case is unknown; whether Marin et al.'s product meets them is unresolved. Ledrappier's content (bound vs partial equality) rests on conflicting secondary sources. The statement does not fix which dimension or quantifier is meant, which affects whether the product example counts against it.
